title: Name the part each clue comes from
statement: When a lesson cites evidence from a text told in parts, name the part and recall the moment by what happens, not by a position like 'the middle'.
detail: Curriculum rulings of 3 July 2026 in the Grade 3 procedure spec, quoted in the reading course renderer, say every reference to story evidence names its part, such as 'In the second part…' or 'By the end of the story…', and never calls a part that is not the final one 'the last part' (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/modelling-moment-procedures.md`, line 866). The spec's routine for finding evidence recalls the moment to re-read as content, what happened and what the character was like, never as a position such as 'in the middle' (line 842). Both are design rules; nothing measured their effect.

evidence.quote: every reference to story evidence names its part ('In the second part…', 'By the end of the story…'); never 'the last part' for a non-final part.
I remember [the moment, recalled as CONTENT - what happened, what the character was like - never as a position like 'in the middle'].
